title: Review: Electron transfer reactions

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Salt bridge
items.clue: Completes the circuit by allowing ions to move between the two solutions.

items.label: Fuel cell
items.clue: Reactants are supplied continuously and products removed, so it never runs down.

items.label: Primary cell
items.clue: Single-use voltaic device: its spontaneous redox reaction cannot be reversed by charging.

items.label: Secondary cell
items.clue: Rechargeable: an external supply reverses the half-equations that occur during discharge.

questions.stem:
A student places three metals, X, Y and Z, in solutions of each other's nitrates. X forms a coating in solutions of Y²⁺ and of Z²⁺; Y forms a coating in the solution of Z²⁺ only; Z shows no change in either solution.
Which of these is the strongest oxidizing agent?

options.text: the ion Z²⁺
the ion X²⁺
the metal X
the metal Z

questions.explanation: Z is oxidized least readily (it displaces neither of the others), so its ion, Z²⁺, is the most readily reduced: it accepts electrons from both X and Y. That makes Z²⁺ the strongest oxidizing agent.

questions.stem: Which equation correctly represents the reaction of aluminium with dilute hydrochloric acid?

options.text: Al(s) + 3HCl(aq) → AlCl₃(aq) + H₂(g)
2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) → 2AlCl₃(aq) + 3H₂(g)
2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) → 2AlCl₃(aq) + 6H(g)
Al(s) + 3HCl(aq) → AlCl₃(aq) + H₂O(l)

questions.explanation: Aluminium forms Al³⁺, so the salt is AlCl₃, and the H⁺ ions are reduced to diatomic hydrogen. Balancing: 2 Al, 6 H and 6 Cl on each side.

questions.stem:
A voltaic cell is made from a Zn(s)|Zn²⁺(aq) half-cell and a Cu(s)|Cu²⁺(aq) half-cell. Zinc is oxidized more readily than copper.
Which statement about the zinc electrode is correct?

options.text: It is positive, as oxidation takes place at a positive anode.
It is the cathode, as positive zinc ions are formed there.
It is negative, as zinc is oxidized there and releases electrons.
It is the cathode, as the oxidation of zinc atoms takes place there.

questions.explanation: Oxidation (Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻) makes zinc the anode, and the electrons it releases into the wire make it the negative electrode of the voltaic cell.

questions.stem: A voltaic cell is to be built from a zinc electrode and a copper electrode, joined by a wire and by a salt bridge containing KNO₃(aq). Zinc is to be the anode. What should the half-cell containing the copper electrode consist of?

options.text: Copper dipping into a solution containing Cu²⁺ ions
Copper dipping into a solution of zinc ions, Zn²⁺
Copper dipping into a beaker of distilled water
Copper dipping into KNO₃(aq), the salt bridge solution

questions.explanation: Each half-cell is a metal dipping into a solution of its own ions. At the copper cathode, Cu²⁺ ions from this solution are reduced: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. (The zinc half-cell is likewise zinc dipping into Zn²⁺(aq).)

questions.stem: Which statement about fuel cells, primary cells and secondary cells is correct?

options.text: A fuel cell supplies electricity for as long as its fuel and oxygen are supplied.
A secondary cell stores electricity, which it releases unchanged on discharge.
A hydrogen fuel cell produces only water, so using one causes no pollution of any kind.
A fuel cell burns its fuel and converts the heat released to electrical energy.

questions.explanation: In a fuel cell the reactants are fed in continuously and the products removed, so it does not run down like a primary or secondary cell, which contains a fixed amount of reactants.

questions.stem: Using positions in the periodic table, which of these metals would be expected to be oxidized most readily?

options.text: lithium
aluminium
rubidium
sodium

questions.explanation: Rubidium is in group 1, period 5. Its single outer electron is far from the nucleus and well shielded, so it is lost most easily; all the other options are higher in a group or further to the right.

questions.stem: Aluminium reacts with excess dilute sulfuric acid. What amount of hydrogen gas is produced when 0.10 mol of aluminium reacts completely?

options.text: 0.10 mol
0.30 mol
0.07 mol
0.15 mol

questions.explanation: Aluminium forms Al³⁺, so the equation is 2Al(s) + 3H₂SO₄(aq) → Al₂(SO₄)₃(aq) + 3H₂(g). 2 mol Al give 3 mol H₂, so 0.10 mol Al gives 0.10 × 3/2 = 0.15 mol H₂.

questions.stem: Molten sodium chloride is electrolysed. Which statement about the electrode connected to the positive terminal of the DC supply is correct?

options.text: It is the anode, where chloride ions lose electrons.
It is the cathode, as the cathode is the positive electrode.
It is the cathode, where chloride ions become oxidized.
It is the anode, where the chloride ions gain electrons.

questions.explanation: The positive electrode draws electrons from the melt: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Oxidation occurs there, so it is the anode; in an electrolytic cell the anode is positive.

questions.stem:
A voltaic cell is made from a Mg(s)|Mg²⁺(aq) half-cell and an Ag(s)|Ag⁺(aq) half-cell. Magnesium is oxidized far more readily than silver.
Which describes the flow of electrons in this cell?

options.text: From Ag to Mg through the wire, since current leaves the positive terminal
From Mg to Ag through the wire, released as Mg atoms are oxidized
From Mg to Ag through the wire, returning to Mg through the salt bridge
From Ag to Mg through the wire, released as Ag⁺ ions are discharged

questions.explanation: Mg → Mg²⁺ + 2e⁻ at the anode releases electrons; they travel through the external wire to the silver cathode, where Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag. Inside the cell, ions carry the charge.

questions.stem:
During discharge of a lead–acid cell, the reaction at the negative electrode is:
Pb(s) + SO₄²⁻(aq) → PbSO₄(s) + 2e⁻
Which half-equation shows the reaction at this electrode while the cell is being charged?

options.text: Pb(s) + SO₄²⁻(aq) → PbSO₄(s) + 2e⁻
PbSO₄(s) → Pb(s) + SO₄²⁻(aq) + 2e⁻
PbSO₄(s) + 2e⁻ → Pb(s) + SO₄²⁻(aq)
Pb(s) + SO₄²⁻(aq) + 2e⁻ → PbSO₄(s)

questions.explanation: Charging reverses the discharge reaction: every species changes side, including the electrons. PbSO₄ is reduced back to Pb, so this electrode is the cathode during charging.

questions.stem: Which statement about the relative ease of reduction of the halogens is correct?

options.text: Iodine is reduced more readily than bromine, as it is further down group 17.
Bromine is reduced more readily than chlorine, as its nucleus has more protons.
Iodide ions are reduced more readily than iodine, as they are charged.
Chlorine is reduced more readily than bromine, as its atoms are smaller.

questions.explanation: An electron added to the smaller chlorine atom is closer to the nucleus and less shielded, so it is attracted more strongly. Ease of reduction of the halogens increases up group 17.

questions.stem:
A voltaic cell is made from Zn(s)|Zn²⁺(aq) and Cu(s)|Cu²⁺(aq) half-cells joined by a salt bridge containing KNO₃(aq). Zinc is the anode.
Which describes how charge moves through the salt bridge?

options.text: Electrons move through it from the zinc half-cell to the copper half-cell.
NO₃⁻ ions move to the copper half-cell, attracted by its positive electrode.
Zn²⁺ ions pass through it to be deposited on the copper electrode.
K⁺ ions move to the copper half-cell and NO₃⁻ ions to the zinc half-cell.

questions.explanation: Zn²⁺ is produced in the zinc half-cell and Cu²⁺ removed from the copper half-cell. Nitrate ions move to the zinc side and potassium ions to the copper side to keep both solutions neutral.
